CanvasElementV11.description: 1.0.0's element, plus the typed options the item table and totals block need.
CanvasElementV11.title: CanvasElementV11

CanvasPageV11.description:
Page *setup* — margins and the editor's grid.

**Paper size and orientation are deliberately absent.** They live on the template row
(``paper_size``, ``page_orientation``, ``page_width_mm``, ``page_height_mm``), which is
where they are ``DECIMAL(19,4)`` and where ``CUSTOM`` is validated to carry both
dimensions. 1.0.0 restated size and orientation inside the tree as well — in the opposite
case — which gave one document two answers to "what paper is this?" and nothing to
resolve them with. One source of truth; see the decision log.
CanvasPageV11.title: CanvasPageV11

CanvasSectionV11.description: 1.0.0's section, with the millimetre box the editor outlines and selects.
CanvasSectionV11.title: CanvasSectionV11

CanvasStyle.description: Typed styling. The renderer composes CSS from these; none of it is CSS itself.
CanvasStyle.title: CanvasStyle

CanvasV10.description:
The ``1.0.0`` root layout tree — **frozen**.

Not kept for politeness. A version row stores this tree verbatim and a
``layout_digest`` over those exact bytes (docs/invoice-design.md §4.3), so a reprint of a
published document verifies against them. Widening this model would make every stored
1.0.0 layout re-validate against a different shape, and *normalising* one on read would
change its digest and silently invalidate the evidence. New capability goes in a new
schema version beside this one; nothing here moves again.
CanvasV10.title: CanvasV10

PrintAsset.description:
An image a layout names, with its bytes when it can print.

``status`` says why bytes are absent, so the renderer refuses with the reason instead of
printing a page without the picture: ``WITHDRAWN`` (deactivated since it was placed),
``TOO_LARGE`` (over the one-image bound), ``OVER_BUDGET`` (the layout's images together
are over their bound), ``MISSING`` (not this company's) or ``UNAVAILABLE`` (its stored
bytes cannot be read or no longer match their digest: an operator's fault, not the author's).
PrintAsset.title: PrintAsset

PrintOptions.description: How many copies print, and what each is marked as.
PrintOptions.title: PrintOptions

PrintPreview.description: A saved version printed once for a person checking it, published or not (§8 R4).
PrintPreview.title: PrintPreview

ResolveTemplateResponse.description:
The resolved layout, and the rule that chose it.

``assignment_rule_id`` is ``None`` when no rule matched and the company's single
published template was used instead — which is the difference between "configured"
and "defaulted", and an operator needs to see it.
ResolveTemplateResponse.title: ResolveTemplateResponse

RowOptions.description: How the body rows of an item table are drawn.
RowOptions.title: RowOptions

TemplateCreated.description:
What creation returns: the template, and the version it created, if any.

A created template is ``DRAFT`` with no live version, so ``current_version_id`` is
null — the designer needs the id of the draft version it just saved, and making the
client list versions to find it would be a worse contract.
TemplateCreated.title: TemplateCreated

post.description:
Upload a brand asset's bytes to this service's own private disk.

The storage path is derived, never supplied; size, digest and (for PNG) pixel
dimensions are measured from the decoded bytes, never taken from the request
(designer plan P4/D3, 2026-11-03 — docs/invoice-design.md §9.2).

delete.description: Withdraw an asset from new layouts. Published layouts keep rendering it.

get.description: One asset, including where this service stored it, and a fresh download token.

The asset's bytes, only against a signed, expiring, actor-bound token.

Current authorization is re-checked here, same as every other read — a token is
never itself the authority, only a bounded convenience once authority is confirmed
(CLAUDE.md §5.14).
The routing rules in force, newest first; with ``template_id``, where one design is used.
